queries:
SELECT s.insurstat AS insurstat,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.zoneregistry) AS site_count,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.zoneregistry) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT s.zoneregistry)) OVER () AS share
FROM scanconservation sc
JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
GROUP BY s.insurstat;
SELECT COALESCE(s.presstat, 'Missing') AS presstat, COUNT(*) AS record_count
FROM scanconservation sc
LEFT JOIN sites s ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
GROUP BY COALESCE(s.presstat, 'Missing');
SELECT COALESCE(s.insurstat, 'Missing') AS insurstat, COUNT(*) AS record_count
FROM scanconservation c
INNER JOIN sites s ON c.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
GROUP BY COALESCE(s.insurstat, 'Missing');
WITH c AS (
  SELECT s.insurstat AS insurstat, COUNT(DISTINCT s.zoneregistry) AS cnt
  FROM sites s
  JOIN scanconservation sc ON sc.zoneref = s.zoneregistry
  GROUP BY s.insurstat
)
SELECT insurstat, 100.0 * cnt / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM c) AS share
FROM c;

Records with a null zoneref are excluded, or counted as their own group. (zoneref is NOT NULL, so this can't happen.)
The share is computed with a window function over the grouped counts, versus a separate subquery total. The result is the same.
The distinct count includes only sites whose conservation records have non-null fields such as harmassess or curerank. This is less literal.

Of these, only the first is a genuinely distinct reading, and it is moot given the NOT NULL constraint. The rest produce identical results, so the existing list is effectively complete.
